newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU assembly condemns EU inaction over Albania.
newsitem.headline: EU assembly condemns EU inaction over Albania.

text.p: The European Parliament criticised European Union governments on Thursday for failing to act together to tackle the crisis in Albania, saying all countries in the 15-member bloc should shoulder the burden.

A resolution deplored the "failure to decide on any joint action...to provide for an adequate protection force for the rapid distribution of humanitarian aid and to contribute actively to the restoration of civil order and the respect of law in Albania".

An Italian-led multinational force, involving troops from Italy, France, Spain, Turkey, Greece and Romania, is expected to start arriving in Albania on Monday to protect the delivery of emergency food and medical supplies.

During a debate on the Albanian crisis in the EU assembly on Wednesday, Euro-deputies complained that by leaving Italy to shoulder the main burden for tackling the crisis, other EU governments were putting Rome under serious domestic pressure.

Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi won support late on Wednesday to send Italian troops to Albania but at the cost of a rift with his hard left allies that will expose his government to a confidence test in parliament.

"An active EU policy towards...Albania is essential in order to provide the necessary humanitarian assistance, restore security in the country and prevent the conflict from spreading to neighbouring countries," the assembly's resolution said.

Albania's Socialist Prime Minister Bashkim Fino told Reuters on Wednesday the 6,000-man contingent was needed to secure Albania's main ports and airport while giving the emergency government time to reorganise its scattered, demoralised security forces.
The parliament said it also wanted the EU actively to contribute to free and fair elections in Albania, the restoration of press freedom and the creation of an independent judicial system.

Earlier on Thursday, Albania's right-wing President Sali Berisha was quoted by an Austrian newspaper as saying he could not be certain that parliamentary elections in the crisis-torn Balkan state would go ahead as planned in June.

Albania, Europe's poorest country, plunged into near chaos when get-rich-quick pyramid investment schemes collapsed and armed rebels took control of the south during an unchecked spasm of looting and banditry.
More than 200 people have been killed and about 700 injured in the violence. Army arsenals were looted after soldiers and police abandoned their posts and citizens seized thousands of weapons.
